so_what: ENOTS leads at 5-2 on the league's 10th-ranked projected roster with 3 FAAB left, and the week hit his starters: Breece Hall has missed four straight, Jaylen Waddle left Week 7 hurt, and Tyler Warren sat again. He cannot buy a fix on the wire, so a trade is his only lever.

Sladsous is 3-4 with the league's most points (960), and Lamar Jackson is reported likely back at Buffalo. A healthy Jackson brings back the rushing that a 4-point pass TD format pays most for, which makes the best-scoring team in the league a live threat for the 6th seed. McCaffrey's mild strain only costs him a bye week.

DiaperDutyDaddy (3-4, 5 FAAB) has the most volatile backfield in the league: Barkley lasted nine snaps on Monday with a new back injury, while Tony Pollard's three-TD day and Woody Marks at 89% of Houston's snaps cover for it. Kamara's every-down role in New Orleans adds a fourth back. With 5 dollars he can only trade, and RB is the one thing he can spare.

Seattle's backfield is about to split three ways: Zach Charbonnet (DadKing) practices fully this week, Jadarian Price (StoneBone69) returns from IR, and mfkr's Emanuel Wilson is the one who loses snaps when they do.

StoneBone69 (4-3, 28 FAAB) ranks last in projected RB points and now gets Price back from IR, but Mike Evans (Achilles/ribs) sat Week 7 and his TE ranks 8th. With 28 dollars he is priced out of any contested claim.

bwalsh89 is last at 2-5 with 64 FAAB. Puka Nacua is his one locked asset, with Davante Adams on IR feeding him more targets, but Cam Skattebo's hamstring and Ladd McConkey's concussion leave the rest thin. At 2-5 he is the owner most likely to take a 2-for-1 trade now.

Stipe's Jahmyr Gibbs aggravated his ankle on 34 touches, but Dan Campbell says he should be good, and Josh Jacobs is back leading Green Bay's backfield. Stipe's real gap is TE (10th of 10) while Dallas Goedert plays through a thin Eagles offense.
